text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple runtime OOMs on us-west-2 shard-9 during high tail load. Paging oncall: maya_oncall. Possible customer impact: streaming timeouts and 5xx increases. Thread started 1860024680

maya_oncall: acknowledging. I'm pulling logs and telemetry. tagging @sarah_sre and @lee_gpu for memory maps. Has anyone rotated the KV cache policy recently?

sarah_sre: I'm around. quick check — is this limited to one pool or across multiple host groups? :eyes:

lee_gpu: initial glance shows 4/16 nodes in pool_g4dn_9 with sudden high allocations around 10:47 UTC. nvidia-smi shows large numbers of small free fragments and intermittent driver GC warnings.

maya_oncall: mitigation action 1: temporarily scale down per-worker max_concurrent_streams 16->8 on pool_g4dn_9 and set per-model max_batch_tokens from 50000->25000. Applying now and will drain two worst nodes.

deploy-bot: runtime-config update queued by maya_oncall (1860024692). Draining nodes: {i-0d9,i-0da} and rolling restart scheduled.

jamal_eng: can we enable an emergency KV-eviction for inactive models? I can throttle cache retention to free headroom.

maya_oncall: enabling immediate KV eviction for models idle > 3m. Patch applied. Observing metrics in 30s.

olivia_prod: PSR: Customer ticket #5492 (BetaCorp) reporting 'generation stalled' from 10:46-10:55 UTC. I'm notifying client-facing teams and will send interim update in 15m.

lee_gpu: memmap snapshot from i-0d9 (excerpt):
```
Total GPU 24GB
Used 21.2GB
Free fragments: [2MB x 40, 8MB x 10, 64MB x 1]
Largest contiguous free: 64MB
Estimated largest needed chunk: 128MB (KV + activations)
Fragmentation index: 0.78
```

maya_oncall: that's consistent with allocation failures for KV pages. Trying immediate node restart after drain to clear fragmentation. Restarting i-0d9 now.

sarah_sre: also enable RUNTIME_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 for a short window to capture allocator stacks on failed allocations. Jamal can you run a targeted repro with long-context prompts against a canary node?

jamal_eng: starting repro against canary i-canary-3. Will push a light patch to allocator that attempts quick coalescing of free pages on deallocation path (alloc-coalesce small heuristic). Pushing to branch `hotfix/alloc-coalesce-186002`.

deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix/alloc-coalesce-186002 -> staging (1860024710) by jamal_eng.

lee_gpu: driver logs on i-0d9 before restart:
```
[10:48:12] driver WARN NVML fragmentation hint: unable to coalesce
[10:48:13] kernel INFO GPU process killed pid=4123 oom
```

maya_oncall: i-0d9 restart complete. Alloc-fail logs decreasing on that host. However i-0da still showing fragmentation spikes. Draining and restarting i-0da now.

natalie_ml: hypothesis: sustained large-context traffic + overlapping stream windows cause many small KV allocations interleaved with frees; allocator's free-list isn't coalescing fast enough, leaving many small fragments that can't satisfy bigger contiguous KV requests. Secondary: upstream driver may delay physical coalesce.

sarah_sre: timeline so far:
- 10:46 alert: runtime alloc-fail spike
- 10:47 observed increases in 5xx and support ticket #5492
- 10:48 quick mitigations: reduced concurrency/batch tokens, enabled KV-eviction for idle models
- 10:49 drain/restart i-0d9 -> seen improvement
- 10:52 repro and alloc debug enabled, hotfix deployed to staging

maya_oncall: short-term plan:
- keep reduced concurrency & batch on the pool for 6 hours
- continue draining unhealthy nodes for restart
- monitor error rate and 95th latency; if error rate >3% reopen paging

olivia_prod: customer comms: sent initial notice to BetaCorp and other impacted accounts. Logged follow-up request for logs; uploaded internal logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1860024680 (internal link).

jamal_eng: staging repro shows the alloc-coalesce patch reduces fragmentation in bench runs. Will open PR with runtime unit tests. If CI green, propose canary to one node in pool_g4dn_9.

sarah_sre: agree to canary after CI. Lee, keep memmap sampling every 3m and paste latest snapshots here.

lee_gpu: memmap sampling 10:57 snapshots:
- i-canary-3 (post-patch): largest_free_chunk 180MB, fragmentation index 0.32
- i-0da (pre-restart): largest_free_chunk 48MB, fragmentation index 0.81

natalie_ml: longer-term mitigations for RCA doc: implement aggressive KV compaction background sweeper, add fragmentation-aware autoscaling rule to keep a % of largest contiguous chunk free, and consider allocator redesign to prefer slab allocations for KV pages.

maya_oncall: handoff soon. Leaving checklist:
- (done) reduced concurrency and batch tokens
- (done) KV eviction enabled for idle models
- (done) drained & restarted two nodes
- (in-progress) repro & alloc patch testing (jamal_eng)
- (todo) canary patch to production pool after CI
- (todo) provider driver bug follow-up if fragmentation persists

deploy-bot: config change applied: pool_g4dn_9 max_concurrent_streams=8, max_batch_tokens=25000 by maya_oncall (1860024726)

sarah_sre: taking over. Jamal, please post PR link and CI status here. I'll create the incident RCA ticket and assign owners: allocator (jamal_eng), KV compaction (natalie_ml), platform autoscale (platform-team). I'll also draft customer-facing RCA outline.

jamal_eng: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/runtime/pull/8721 (alloc-coalesce hotfix). CI: running, currently 4/12 tests failing due to unrelated flakiness, running again.

lee_gpu: one more datapoint: if load is sustained, fragmentation creeps back up over ~20-30m based on previous incidents. That suggests background coalescing or proactive eviction is required instead of restarts every time.

olivia_prod: I'll keep BetaCorp informed and will send an update after canary results. Flagging support tickets for SLA review.

sarah_sre: closing this paging handoff. Current status: SEV3, customer impact diminished. Monitoring window open. If error rate >2.5% or 95th latency >2s on pool_g4dn_9, paging triggers. Incident ID: 1860024680

jamal_eng: will follow up with PR updates.

maya_oncall: signing off from oncall. Thanks for the assist. :white_check_mark:

-- end of thread --
